# A test reaches through an #id named like a component, on every target: the
# one it names (`card #card`), through its state (`c.card.hits`) and its node
# (`c.card.btn.click()`), and another the body still renders by name
# (`cell #box` beside `box()`).

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok   2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:test"

component card ui.node {
    var hits = 0
    ui.button #btn(text="hit", @click {
        hits = hits + 1
    })
}

component main ui.node {
    card #card()
}

func testReadsThroughAnIDNamedLikeItsComponent(t test.Test, c main) {
    c.card.btn.click()
    t.assert(c.card.hits == 1)
}

component box ui.node {
    ui.text(value="box")
}

component cell(name string) ui.node {
    var got = name
}

component pair ui.node {
    cell #box(name="a")
    cell #other(name="b")
    box()
}

func testAnIDNamedLikeAnotherComponent(t test.Test, c pair) {
    t.assert(c.box.got == "a")
    t.assert(c.other.got == "b")
}

ui.window {
    main()
}
